standard_prerequisites.name: Integral ring extensions have no inclusion of prime ideals and their spectra are totally disconnected
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemmas algebra-lemma-integral-no-inclusion (tag 00GS) and algebra-lemma-ring-with-only-minimal-primes (tag 00G3)
standard_prerequisites.use: These give that every prime of the integral closure is minimal and maximal, which is what makes the constancy argument work.

standard_prerequisites.name: Morphisms into affine schemes and the characterization of local rings
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Schemes, Lemma schemes-lemma-morphism-into-affine (tag 01I1); Algebra, Lemma algebra-lemma-characterize-local-ring (tag 00ER)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first factors the structure morphism through Spec(k') and the second identifies k' as local once all elements outside p are units.

core_obligations: Let k' be the integral closure of k in Gamma(X, O_X) and factor X -> Spec(k) through Spec(k'), noting that k' has no nonzero nilpotents because X is reduced (proof lines 5327-5330).
Use integrality of k -> k' to see that every prime ideal of k' is simultaneously maximal and minimal, so that Spec(k') is totally disconnected (proof lines 5331-5335).

Use connectedness of X to conclude that X -> Spec(k') is constant with image the point corresponding to a prime p of k', and that any f in k' outside p maps to an invertible element of O_X and therefore is a unit of k' (proof lines 5336-5340).
Conclude that k' is local with maximal ideal p, and since k' is reduced it is a field (proof lines 5341-5345).
proof_roadmap: Factor the structure morphism through the integral closure of the ground field.
Show the spectrum of that closure is totally disconnected.
Use connectedness to make the morphism constant and identify the units.
Conclude that the closure is local and reduced, hence a field.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a connected reduced scheme X over a field k, the integral closure k' of k inside Gamma(X, O_X) is a field. The proof observes that X -> Spec(k) factors through Spec(k'), that k' is reduced because X is, and that by integrality of k -> k' every prime of k' is both minimal and maximal so Spec(k') is totally disconnected (proof lines 5327-5335). It then uses connectedness of X to see the morphism X -> Spec(k') is constant with image a point p, so that any f in k' not in p maps to an invertible element of O_X and hence is a unit of k'; k' is therefore local with maximal ideal p, and being reduced it is a field (proof lines 5336-5345). H2: the route from total disconnectedness of Spec(k') through constancy of the map to the locality of k' is the substance.
